subject: Re: Acme POC — access, success criteria, and timeline
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-27T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Acme POC — access, success criteria, and timeline

Hi Jordan — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

1) Success criteria (Agreed):
   - Generate representative chat completions for support workflows with >= 90% parity to current responses (sample set attached).
   - End-to-end request latency < 400ms p50 and < 1s p95 for 512-token case.
   - Cost per 1k tokens below your current vendor baseline — we'll run identical prompts to compare.

2) POC scope & timeline:
   - Week 0 (this week): Access + baseline dataset ingest.
   - Week 1: Run initial runs, measure latency & quality.
   - Week 2: Iterate on prompt set and quant/profile settings.
   - Week 3: Final run and scorecard; decision meeting.

3) Owners:
   - Redwood (point): me (Marissa) — commercial/coordination.
   - Redwood (tech): Vivek — test harness, baseline runs.
   - Acme: Jordan — provide dataset samples and approve success criteria.

4) Access required (ACTION for Acme IT):
   - API key: we will issue a scoped API key for the POC.
   - IP allowlist: please provide the CIDR(s) for your network or allowlists for their side if needed.
   - SSO invites: if you prefer SSO for team members, let us know emails for invite.

I've attached the quickstart and a mapping template for your dataset. Next step: Jordan, can you provide an initial sample of ~200 transcripts and the IP ranges for your staging environment by EOD Thursday (2026-03-02)? We'll provision API credentials as soon as we have that.

Thanks!
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-poc-quickstart.pdf (6MB stub), acme-mapping-template.xlsx (12KB stub)

- For the scoped API key, can you restrict it to the POC project and limit rate to 10 rps?
- Do you need service account creds for automated baseline runs, or is a single API key sufficient?

Hey Jordan — quick answers below. Happy to jump on a short call with your IdP folks if helpful.

- Scoped API key: yes, we can issue a POC-limited API key scoped to a single project and set a rate limit (10 rps) and token quota.
- Service account vs API key: for automated baseline runs, we recommend a service account-style key (rotatable) — we can issue one that lives in the customer's private project/access boundary for the Private deployment, but for hosted POC we'll provision a scoped API key.
- Endpoint: yes, we can provision a us-west-2 non-prod endpoint (hosted) for the POC. We'll confirm region-level routing.

Action items for Redwood (Vivek): provision scoped API key, create non-prod endpoint, and share onboarding steps by Tue 2026-03-03.

-Vivek

Jordan — adding a couple of notes on evaluation plan and scoring so expectations are clear:

- We'll run the 200 transcripts through the Redwood evaluation harness (same prompts you use in prod). Output will be scored against your golden set with both automated metrics (BLEU/EM-like similarity where appropriate) and human spot-checks for correctness.
- Timeline: once we have data and creds, plan is 48 hours for baseline runs, then 48 hours for optimization round. Final scorecard delivered as a Google Sheet.
- Decision criteria: pass if automated score within 10% of current baseline and no major functional regressions in human spot-checks.

I will own the scorecard delivery. Vivek will own infra/provisioning. Marissa will own timeline and commercial follow-ups.

Thanks — Nikhil
